title: What If the 1918 Flu Came Back? It Infected One in Three People

scenes.text: What if the 1918 flu came back? It infected one in three people on Earth.
That was about 500 million people. At least 50 million died, nearly 3 percent of humanity.
It hit young adults hard. Healthy twenty- to forty-year-olds died in large numbers, which is unusual for flu.
Many deaths were likely from bacterial pneumonia that followed the flu, and 1918 had no antibiotics to treat it.
There was no flu vaccine either. Today we have both antibiotics and flu vaccines.
The virus wasn't the only killer. A world without those tools was.

description:
What if the 1918 flu returned?
It infected about one in three people and killed at least 50 million. No vaccine, no antibiotics. Much of the toll came from bacterial pneumonia, which today's medicine can treat.
